newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate rises, baht weaker late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate rises, baht weaker late.

text.p: Tighter liquidity pushed the Thai overnight interbank rate up to 9.50-10.00 percent in late trade on Thursday from 8.50 percent earlier, dealers said.
Dealers attributed the tightening money supply to money leaving the market to buy the rising dollar over the past few days.
"Fund flowed out to buy the U.S. unit and have not yet returned to the market," said one dealer at a U.S. bank.
The baht was lower to 25.481-25.486 to the dollar late from 25.475-25.480 early reflecting the dollar's movement abroad, dealers said.
"There was continued buying of the dollar today. But it was not as strong as over the past few days," said one currency dealer.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium was at 8.00/9.00 satangs per dollar late compared with 8.00/8.50 in early morning.
The mid-rate was fixed unchanged at 25.47 to the dollar.
